clue.text: Spotted, we hear, mak, ing a nasty row

indicators.note: we hear says the word for spotted is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: spotted means seen, as in caught sight of

explanation.surface: Someone is overheard kicking up an ugly quarrel in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'making' broken as 'mak, ing'; it is only a link word. A SCENE is a noisy public row.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a scene means causing a loud embarrassing public fuss or quarrel.

clue.text: Awful to use very tired slave labour

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grumble that it is dreadful to work exhausted slaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges USE, V and TIRED; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Servitude is the condition of being bound to forced work, the lot of a slave.

clue.text: A novel way to sign a letter

definitions.meaning: Jane Austen wrote a novel of this name
in the old signallers' alphabet the letter M was spoken by this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign a letter' suggests putting a name at the foot of a letter; here it means signalling the letter M, which old army signallers called by this name (as in 'pip emma' for p.m.).
explanation.definitionFit: Austen's novel Emma, and Emma as the old phonetic signal for the letter M.

clue.text: He was victorious, we re told

definitions.text: He was victorious, we re told

parts.words: He was victorious, we re told
parts.note: read as 'he was Victoria's', the clue describes the husband of a queen regnant, namely Albert, husband of Queen Victoria

explanation.surface: Someone is reported to have won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorious, we're told' sounds like 'Victoria's': he belonged to Victoria. The page prints 'we're' as 'we re'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert was the husband of the reigning Queen Victoria, holding the title given to such a husband.

clue.text: Dance of the panto mime horse?

definitions.text: Dance of the panto mime horse?

parts.words: Dance of the panto mime horse?
parts.note: slang for dancing, and a pantomime horse's legs end in a horse's foot

explanation.surface: A question about how the two-person horse costume in a Christmas show dances.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show; its horse is two actors in one costume. The page prints 'pantomime' as 'panto mime'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoofing is slang for dancing, and a horse stands on its hooves.

clue.text: Nose around — nothing useable as rope

indicators.note: around says the first word is wrapped round the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone's nose is sniffing about, and nothing found is any good as rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot, as on a hangman's rope.

clue.text: You can get real money for this land

parts.note: taken as written; the answer also runs across the words real money, a coincidence of the charade

explanation.surface: A country where your cash buys genuine value.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, a land ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Courageous to put on "The Tempest and face hostility

parts.note: courageous means brave
taken as written
a tempest is a storm

explanation.surface: A theatre company boldly staging Shakespeare's play The Tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tempest' looks like Shakespeare's play; split it into THE and a synonym. 'to put on' is a link. The page drops the closing quote mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave the storm is an idiom for facing up to opposition or anger.

clue.text: Caesar beware the side turn!

indicators.note: turn tells us to twist the letters of side into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning to Caesar to watch out for the side turning.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar was warned 'Beware the Ides of March', so the first words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's soothsayer told Julius Caesar to beware the Ides of March, the day he was killed.

clue.text: It's really the end to feed us such a cheap cut!

definitions.text: It's really the end to feed us such a cheap cut!

parts.words: It's really the end to feed us such a cheap cut!
parts.note: a diner's complaint about being served the bony neck end of mutton, the cheapest joint

explanation.surface: A diner protests at being served poor-quality meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end' hints that this cut is the neck end of a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag is the bony neck end of mutton, one of the cheapest cuts of meat.

clue.text: Some moist yellow salve for eye-sore

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A damp yellow ointment for a sore eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salve for' is a link reading: the hidden word is what is salved, the eye-sore itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Start on stone work

indicators.note: work suggests the letters are worked into a new shape, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A mason begins on the masonry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'stonework' as 'stone' worked; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is a beginning, the start of something.

clue.text: Rear Admiral's vessel, for example, has one

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a boat is its back end

definitions.text: Admiral's vessel, for example, has one
definitions.meaning: any ship, an admiral's flagship included, has a back end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear Admiral' looks like a naval rank, but 'Rear' is the first definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the back part of a ship, so it is the rear, and every vessel has one.

clue.text: Scrupulous and aware of outstanding debts

parts.note: conscient is an old word meaning aware or conscious
IOUs are written promises of money still owed

explanation.surface: Someone careful and mindful of what they still owe.
explanation.walkthrough: CONSCIENT is an old word for 'aware'; 'and' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscientious person is careful and principled, guided by conscience.

clue.text: The second sage ex presses it differently

parts.note: second, as in a second one, means other
sage means wise

explanation.surface: A second wise man puts the point another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' and 'expresses it' are link words; the page prints 'expresses' as 'ex presses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in a different way or differently.

clue.text: Apprentice getting spells of work

parts.note: recalls the tale of the ... apprentice, and the masters whose work is casting spells

explanation.surface: A trainee gets occasional bursts of employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spells of work' looks like periods of work; it means magic spells, the work of the masters in Dukas's 'The Sorcerer's Apprentice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Magicians whose trade is casting spells, as in the tale of the apprentice who misused one.

clue.text: After Easter, find new place of worship for Orthodox sect

parts.note: taken as written
a church is a place of worship

explanation.surface: After the Easter holiday, someone looks for a new church to join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' and 'find' are link words; the pieces run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orthodox churches of eastern Europe and Asia are known together as the Eastern Church.

clue.text: Halt at this point

definitions.meaning: to halt is to come to a standstill
a full ... marks the point where a sentence ends

explanation.definitionFit: Stop means halt, and a stop is the full point that ends a sentence.

clue.text: Tear off a sports outfit in a fury?

definitions.meaning: to tear off is to peel away or rip off
a team's matching kit is called its colours in British use

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a fury?' points to the idiom 'tear someone off a strip', to scold them angrily; in Britain a team's kit is its strip.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to tear off a covering, and a strip is a football team's kit.

clue.text: Major player to head organisation?

indicators.note: to head says we take the leading part of the word organisation

explanation.surface: A key figure is promoted to lead the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major player' looks like an important person; it is the large musical instrument found in churches.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is a large instrument, often the grandest player in a church.

clue.text: Immoral, slack…

definitions.meaning: immoral in the sense of promiscuous or dissolute
slack means not tight, hanging free

explanation.definitionFit: Loose describes both lax morals and something not tightly fixed.

clue.text: … and follow one's fancy, with a foot on 22

definitions.text: … and follow one's fancy, with a foot on 22

parts.words: … and follow one's fancy, with a foot on 22
parts.note: continues the previous clue into the phrase footloose and fancy-, with foot placed before the answer to 22

explanation.surface: Someone does as they please, wandering without ties.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on from 22-across: put 'foot' on 22 for 'footloose', and the saying is 'footloose and fancy-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fancy-free means unattached and at liberty to follow one's whims.

clue.text: Heard Alfred's on Cole ridge's sacred river

indicators.note: heard says the short name is to be taken as spoken

parts.note: Alf is the short form of Alfred

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have heard Alfred talking about Coleridge's holy river.
explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's poem 'Kubla Khan', 'Alph, the sacred river, ran'. The page prints 'Coleridge's' as 'Cole ridge's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge names the sacred river of Xanadu in his poem Kubla Khan.

clue.text: A couch, or in it

parts.note: a couch is something to lie on, a bed

explanation.surface: A couch, or perhaps lying on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to the couch: to be in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed is an old word for in bed.

clue.text: Opera role got it changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer's part in an opera has been revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opera role' reads as one phrase, but 'Opera' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's opera about a court jester.

clue.text: Sea-water is a cure

definitions.meaning: salt water is used to cure and preserve food such as pickles and ham

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure' suggests a remedy; it means preserving food.
explanation.definitionFit: Brine is salty water, like the sea, and the solution used for pickling.

clue.text: Belief in one God gone to pot?

definitions.text: Belief in one God gone to pot?

indicators.note: gone to says the belief is placed after the pot

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
theism is belief in a single god

explanation.surface: A wry question whether faith in one God has gone to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone to pot' means ruined; read literally, the belief goes to the pot. The ? flags the jocular reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism holds that God is everything and everywhere, belief spread thinly, as if gone to pot.

clue.text: Uniform style may go full circle

definitions.meaning: formal military wear, as in full ceremonial uniform
to style hair is to arrange it
it can follow the word full and precede the word circle

explanation.walkthrough: Full dress is ceremonial uniform; the dress circle is a theatre's first balcony.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress means a uniform, to style hair, and joins full or circle in fixed phrases.
